description: §17.1 / §42.4 statement 10: `if=!g()` with `g()` unresolved is E-COND-NOT-BOOLEAN (annotate `g` `-> bool`, or write `if=!(g() is given)`).
rationale:
§42.4 statement 10: "`

` … with `g` declaring no return type" is E-COND-NOT-BOOLEAN. Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S460 "a on F2, go". S478 (bootstrap triage F1): `g` now returns a value typed `asIs`, one of statement 5's own unresolved sources ("a value typed `asIs` / `unknown` (§7.5.2)"; the §42.4 worked example's `u: asIs`), so `g()`'s return type is neither declared nor inferred. The earlier `function g() { }` no longer tests this: "a call of a function that returns nothing is not a value (§48 \"The return rule\", rule 3; E-TYPE-001 in a value position)" (§4.14; S469 "fall-off and tail returns: ALWAYS EXPLICIT"), so `g()` is E-TYPE-001 inside the condition, and §42.4 statement 6 ("No second report": no statement-5 report "when the compiler has already reported any Error-severity diagnostic whose span lies within the condition") then rightly suppresses E-COND-NOT-BOOLEAN.
